_note: Matched-volume series: L grows with beta (12,16,20,24,28,32) to hold the physical box L*sqrt(sigma)a roughly fixed as a->0, suppressing the torelon contamination of the scalar channel. rmax bounds the Cornell-fit r-window at the noise onset of V(r): the last r before the static-potential increments stop decreasing monotonically (V(r) must be concave; the increment -> sigma a^2 from above). Cuts are read directly from the per-point dV(r) table: L24/L28 stay clean through r=7 (jump at r=8), L32 through r=6.
_provisional: The three fine points (beta=2.50/2.55/2.60) now carry high statistics (800k-960k configs at L24/L28; 300k at L32). The 0++ glueball mass m_0 a is well-resolved at all three (sub-2% jackknife). The string tension remains the limiting observable: even at this statistics V(r) loses signal (r~7) before reaching a long clean linear regime, so the Cornell-fit sigma a^2 carries a large jackknife error (~30% at L28, and sigma is effectively undetermined at L32 b2.60 where only 300k configs were collected at the finest/noisiest spacing). The continuum m(0++)/sqrt(sigma) intercept below is therefore consistent with the Teper value but NOT a sharper determination; it is dominated by the sigma uncertainty, not the glueball. A trustworthy sharpening needs more fine-a sigma statistics (larger Wilson-loop extent and/or more configs at L28/L32) so V(r) reaches the asymptotic linear regime with signal.
